nodes.name: Pristine oxide electrodeposition and chalcogenization
nodes.procedure: The fabrication of the MXs involves the electrodeposition of pristine metal oxides (CoO, Co0.5Fe0.5O, Co0.37Ni0.26Fe0.37O) followed by subsequent sulfurization/selenization/tellurization treatments at high temperature to produce the corresponding metal sulfides/selenides/tellurides.
nodes.source_text: The fabrication of the MXs involves the electrodeposition of pristine metal oxides and the subsequent sulfurization/selenization/tellurization treatments at high temperature in order to produce the corresponding metal sulfides/selenides/tellurides (see Experimental Section for details).

nodes.name: In situ electrochemical oxidation tuning

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show CoS₂, CoSe₂, and CoTe₂ exhibit porous nanosheet morphology, while ECT-X-CoO shows nanoporous structures after electrochemical tuning.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of (a) CoS₂, (b) CoSe₂, (c) CoTe₂, and (d) pristine CoO before tuning... SEM images of (i) CoS₂, (j) CoSe₂, (k) CoTe₂, and (l) pristine CoO after the electrochemical tuning.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM of CoSe₂ shows porous nanosheets with mesopores and crystal grain size of tens of nanometers; ECT-Se-CoO exhibits more porous nanostructures with nanopores less than 5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM image that the CoX (CoSe₂ as an example) shows porous nanosheets with numerous mesopores... the ECT-Se-CoO after the in situ electrochemical oxidation tuning of CoSe₂ in 1 M KOH exhibits even more porous nanostructures.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms nanopores in ECT-Se-CoO typically less than 5 nm; Co₀.₃₇Ni₀.₂₆Fe₀.₃₇Se₂ nanoparticles >10 nm with (210) plane fringes, ECT-Se-Co₀.₃₇Ni₀.₂₆Fe₀.₃₇O nanoparticles <5 nm with weak crystallinity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is further demonstrated in HRTEM that the nanopores are typically with size less than 5 nm... these tiny ECT-Se-Co₀.₃₇Ni₀.₂₆Fe₀.₃₇O nanoparticles are mostly less than 5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX of CoSe₂ shows coexistence of Co and Se elements; intensive Se peaks disappear completely in ECT-Se-CoO, confirming successful transformation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDX) of CoSe₂ shows the coexistence of both Co and Se elements... the intensive Se peaks disappear completely in the ECT-Se-CoO.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows pristine CoO crystal structure unchanged after tuning; CoSe₂, CoS₂, and CoTe₂ change from highly crystalline (cubic pyrite phase dominant for CoSe₂) to nearly amorphous structures after tuning.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) were further performed... the electrochemical tuning exhibits significant alternations on the crystal structure of CoX₂, where CoSe₂, CoS₂, and CoTe₂ changed from highly crystalline to nearly amorphous structures.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Se 3d peaks at 55.4 eV (3d₃/₂) and 54.8 eV (3d₅/₂) for Se₂²⁻ in CoSe₂ disappear in ECT-Se-CoO; Co 2p shifts from Co²⁺ (793.5 eV 2p₁/₂, 778.6 eV 2p₃/₂) to Co³⁺ (795.2 eV 2p₁/₂, 780.1 eV 2p₃/₂) in ECT-Se-CoO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks of Se 3d₃/₂ around 55.4 eV and Se 3d₅/₂ around 54.8 eV are in good agreement with Se₂²⁻ in CoSe₂... The binding energies of Co 2p₁/₂ at 795.2 eV and Co 2p₃/₂ at 780.1 eV in ECT-Se-CoO correspond to Co³⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV for electrochemical double layer capacitance measurement shows ECT-S-CoO has areal capacitance of 270 mF cm⁻² and ECT-Se-CoO has 121 mF cm⁻², both superior to pristine CoO at 41 mF cm⁻², indicating higher surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECT-S-CoO and ECT-Se-CoO exhibit high areal capacitances of 270 and 121 mF cm⁻², respectively, superior to that of the pristine CoO with an areal capacitance of 41 mF cm⁻² (Figure S13b).
